cited_details.statement: As Han (2022) notes, "manifold learning is believed to be good at handling nonlinear data and discovering their intrinsic local geometry in the low-dimensional" embedding space, which makes it particularly well suited to multimedia content whose semantic structure is not captured by linear projections [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0925231222007044].

Roweis and Saul (2000) introduced Locally Linear Embedding, an unsupervised learning algorithm that "computes low dimensional, neighborhood preserving embeddings of high" dimensional data [https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Nonlinear-dimensionality-reduction-by-locally-Roweis-Saul/f0a3e1752e1146da927adc24ae07144ab2e744ec].

Tenenbaum, Silva, and Langford (2000) proposed Isomap, a "global geometric framework" that extends classical Multidimensional Scaling by approximating geodesic distances along the data manifold rather than Euclidean distances in the ambient space [https://pdodds.w3.uvm.edu/files/papers/others/2000/tenenbaum2000a.pdf].

According to the source evidence, "Isomap's global coordinates provide a simple way to analyze and manipulate high-dimensional observations in terms of their intrinsic nonlinear" structure, and the paper studies Isomap's performance on both artificial and natural datasets [https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Reduction-A-Global-Geometric-Framework-for-Tenenbaum-Silva/2878f950f0ad19ccec6bab04873895e89f5bece0].

Their presentation observes that "IsoMAP, LLE and Laplacian eigenmaps partially solve" the problem of nonlinear dimensionality reduction, and that "the heart of these approaches is some kind of non-linear method" that targets the intrinsic geometry of the data [https://www.aoml.noaa.gov/ftp/pub/phod/thacker/SSAmanifoldPapers/BelkinNiyogi2007Presentation.pdf].

Wang and colleagues developed a manifold–manifold distance framework specifically for face recognition with image sets, treating each subject's gallery and probe as points on potentially different low-dimensional manifolds and computing a geometric distance between them [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22752133/].

The "Face recognition with image sets using manifold density divergence" approach proposes "a flexible, semiparametric model for learning probability densities confined to highly non-linear but intrinsically low-dimensional manifolds" and recasts recognition as a problem of "minimizing the divergence between densities estimated on these manifolds" [https://research-portal.st-andrews.ac.uk/en/publications/face-recognition-with-image-sets-using-manifold-density-divergenc/].

Pospelov (2021) "examined the efficiency of the named nonlinear manifold learning methods (Isomap, LE and LLE) compared to the linear dimensionality reduction" techniques on fMRI data [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666956021000337].

Han (2022) directly addresses this issue, focusing on how to "enhance explainability of manifold learning" while preserving the method's ability to "handle nonlinear data and discover their intrinsic local geometry in the low-dimensional" space [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0925231222007044].
